sector: Payments / integrated payments for restaurants, hospitality, sports and entertainment, luxury retail and tax-free shopping

horizon_text: End-2029 value on calendar-2029 adjusted EBITDA, undiscounted; no common dividend
thesis: Shift4's adjusted FCF set a quarterly record of $200M in Q3 2026 and the FY2026 FCF guide held, but guidance was cut for the second time this year (GRLNF and adjusted EBITDA about 4% and 6% below the original guide), Q4 adjusted EBITDA is guided 1-6% below Q4 2025, organic GRLNF growth slowed to 8% and organic payments-based growth has been 14% all year. Buybacks of $511M in nine months shrank the share count while net debt rose to $4.30B (3.8x EBITDA), and the preferred converts into 12.5M shares in May 2028. At about 7.4x FY2026 EBITDA, a base of 7% EBITDA growth to 2029 with deleveraging at a 7.0x exit is worth $65.06; weighted toward the bear, about 10% a year.
consensus_view: No current Street snapshot was captured; the May call recorded a $60.81 mean target. At $43.73, down about 40% this year, the market pays about 7.4x guided FY2026 EBITDA for a levered processor whose guidance has been cut twice, which assumes little growth after the Global Blue synergies.
variant_view: No strong variant view. We agree with the market that two guidance cuts, slowing organic growth and debt-funded buybacks earn a discount. Our base differs only in expecting EBITDA to grow again from 2027 as Global Blue synergies land and Tax-Free Shopping recovers, so leverage falls to about 2.5x by 2029 without a re-rating. The checkable test is the 2027 outlook in February: adjusted EBITDA guided at least 6% above FY2026 including Paramount.

notes: The May call used 2030 adjusted FCF multiples and stated the base as its fair value; this update states three-year end-2029 values on 2029 adjusted EBITDA, undiscounted, net of debt, TRA and NCI, with the preferred as converted. The rating rule annualizes over 3 years; end-2029 is 3.14 years away, at which the fair value returns 9.1% a year.

Net debt roll-forward: $4,297M at September 30, 2026, plus Paramount ($143M upfront and the scenario's earnout), less Q4 2026 adjusted FCF ($160M) and 2027-2029 adjusted FCF at the scenario's conversion, plus 3.25 years of integration costs, about $108M of preferred dividends (seven payments of $15.4M to May 2028), $43M of after-tax interest income lost on the $633M of cash that repays the 2027 convertible (assumed 3.75% yield), and $90M a year of buybacks that offset grants (fully diluted common held at 77.76M). The term loan's full-year interest above the FY2026 baseline (about $25M after tax over 2027-2029) is left out, and roughly offsets the operating leverage a flat 42% conversion misses when interest is fixed.
Paramount Commerce's EBITDA is assumed at about $20M from 2027 (the letter says the upfront price is below 8x EBITDA) and is included in every EBITDA path; the EBITDA kill criterion excludes it.

The Series A preferred (10,253,296 shares) converts on May 1, 2028 at 0.9780-1.2224 Class A shares each (10-K FY2025); the maximum rate applies below $81.81, so 12.53M shares in the bear and base. Shift4's non-GAAP EPS counts the preferred one for one.
No current Street consensus snapshot was captured for this update.

capital.multiples gives FOUR's GAAP EV/EBIT of 18.7x against a peer median of 19.0x (CART, DLO, MELI, PAY, PYPL, WU); its P/E and P/FCF histories are not usable because the XBRL diluted share count covers one share class. The exit check is today's EV/EBITDA of about 7.4x on guided FY2026 EBITDA; at 6.5x the base is $57.40 (fair value $53.71), at 7.5x $72.73 (fair value $61.37).
Base EBITDA CAGR of 7.3% sits at about the 66th percentile of revenue growth for its size bucket in library/BASE_RATES.md; the bull's 11.3% at about the 83rd.

First review round (B; evidence 4, valuation 3, variant view 3, risk 3, calibration 3): organic growth was overstated (organic payments-based GRLNF +14%, organic GRLNF +8% in Q3), base integration costs of $40M a year were far below the $109M TTM, the bear counted refinancing twice although the July term loan had already funded the convertible, Paramount's EBITDA was unaddressed, preferred dividends were understated and NCI omitted, the 45% claim on a 2027 guide reaching the base contradicted 70% weight on base and bull, the leverage kill could fire on value-adding buybacks, and the May change-my-mind items were not reported. First draft values were $25.50 / $67.75 / $109.14 at 30/50/20, fair value $63.35, positive bias.
The scenarios are read as bands: bear below about 3% 2027 EBITDA growth, base about 3-9%, bull above 9%; P(2027 guide >= 6%) = half the base plus the bull = 40%, the claim's probability.
why_opportunity is behavioral: the stock is down about 40% this year on two guidance cuts, which the market may extrapolate; the call shares most of that caution and has no strong variant view.

Second review round (B; evidence 4, valuation 4, variant view 3, risk 3, calibration 4): the EBITDA kill excluding Paramount was unobservable, the bear tripped the leverage kill (3.7x) and FCF kill ($460M) only barely, the 40% claim needed the band reading stated, the term loan's carry above the FY2026 baseline was unaddressed, and three May change-my-mind items were unreported. Values were unchanged at $25.68 / $65.06 / $106.80.

low_score_reasons: variant_view: the note says 'No strong variant view' yet tags why_opportunity as behavioral, and its only disagreement (EBITDA grows again in 2027) is checkable but not shown to be something the market is missing.

risk: the EBITDA kill excluded Paramount, whose EBITDA Shift4 does not report, so it could not be resolved from filings; the bear tripped the leverage kill by only 0.02-0.05x (3.72-3.75x against 3.7x) and the FCF kill by only $12M ($448M against $460M).
review.counter_case: Organic payments-based GRLNF grew 14% in every 2026 quarter, and Q3's slide in organic GRLNF growth from 11% to 8% is mostly subscription (organic -1% to -8%), which management says it is deliberately trading for payments revenue; the Q4 EBITDA decline is partly a comparison with an unusual $145M subscription quarter in Q4 2025. The note still puts 35% on a bear in which organic EBITDA falls while the largest segment compounds at 14% and synergies ramp, values that bear at 5.5x with 3.2x leverage, and de-rates the base to 7.0x from today's 7.4x even as leverage falls to 2.5x. Holding 7.4x in the base ($71.20), 6.0x in the bear ($32.13) and 30/50/20 weights gives $66.60, 15.05% a year: Own.
review.response: Accepted the corrections: the EBITDA kill now uses reported figures (FY2027 below FY2026 plus $20M for Paramount); the leverage kill is 3.5x with EBITDA growth below 3%, and the FCF kill $470M, so the bear fires them clearly and the base clears them; the note states the scenarios as bands, which makes the 40% claim the weights' own probability; the term loan's carry and the operating leverage a flat 42% misses are named as roughly offsetting; all six May change-my-mind items are reported; base_rate is filled (66th percentile). On the counter-case: the weights stay 35/50/15 because Shift4 itself guides Q4 EBITDA below last year after two cuts, so a flat 2027 is close to the exit rate, not a remote tail; and a 7.0x exit, a slight de-rating from 7.4x, suits a business whose guidance fell 6% in a year. The note states that a 2027 guide of 8% or more would bring the call close to Own, and February's outlook tests it.
